entry_phrase: The count is of holders, not keys: a holder's primary and backup keys are one holder, under whichever of their keys is live.

gist: No single signer admits an amendment and no single signer vetoes one by refusing to sign; WA quorum is the primary review
entry_phrase: No single signer admits an amendment, and no single signer vetoes one by refusing to sign. The sign-off is the secondary check; WA quorum is the primary substantive review.

gist: Until the scale gate (100000 production agents active in 24 h by census) amendment authority rests with the founder as steward; any accord holder may propose
entry_phrase: The scale gate is the point at which the mesh reaches scale: ≥100,000 production agents active in a 24-hour period, QA and harness agents excluded, measured by the census ([CC 6.1.9](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.9)). **Until the mesh reaches scale, amendment authority rests with the founder as steward, and any accord-holder may propose an amendment**.

gist: Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster; after it governance tightens never loosens
entry_phrase: Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster. After the scale gate governance tightens, never loosens.

gist: The scale gate is amendable by the steward before the gate and only by the entrenched process after it
entry_phrase: The scale gate itself is amendable by the steward before the scale gate. After the scale gate it is amendable only by the [CC 4.5.1.2](#4.5.1.2) entrenched process.

gist: At the scale gate the federation-Contribution and WA-quorum machinery supersedes founder authority
entry_phrase: The federation-Contribution + WA-quorum machinery is **deferred to mechanization** at the scale gate. At that point it *supersedes* founder authority and tightens governance onto the quorum/entrenchment process.

gist: Every clause conferring authority or gating a capability MUST pass the swap test before adoption; a failure is recorded on the declared-asymmetry register
entry_phrase: Every clause that **confers authority or gates a capability** MUST pass the swap test before adoption. The test is this: *swap the most and least powerful parties the clause names or implies, re-read it, and ask whether it still reads acceptable; if it does not, it was a privilege, not a rule*. This is a drafting gate on what CC may say, never an adjudication rule. It binds amendment and the steward's authority before the scale gate alike. Where the test **fails**, the outcome is recorded on the declared-asymmetry register below.

gist: A formally universal gate is not established as substantively equal by passing the swap test; its residual belongs in the clause that imposes it
entry_phrase: A formally universal gate is therefore **not** established as substantively equal by having passed. Where the gate stays mandatory, the residual belongs in the clause that imposes it, not in this one.

gist: An asymmetry escaped by instantiating the form is a default; one surviving instantiation is a privilege; only privileges need justification and go on the register
entry_phrase: An asymmetry a party escapes by **instantiating the form** — naming their own occupants for the slots CC specifies — is a **default**. An asymmetry that **survives instantiation** is a **privilege**. Only privileges require justification, and only privileges belong on this register.

gist: A carried privilege MUST be listed, bounded by an ending condition, revocable by the disadvantaged party unilaterally, and scope-isolated
entry_phrase: A privilege is either rewritten until it passes the swap test, or carried here. A carried privilege MUST satisfy all four:

gist: Two thirds of the sitting WA board confirms members, removes them and amends the charter
entry_phrase: ≥⅔ of the sitting board confirms members, ≥⅔ removes them, ≥⅔ amends the charter

gist: WBD deferral is mandatory and freezes the deferring agent; a deferral MUST NOT be left open
entry_phrase: while WBD deferral is mandatory and freezes the deferring agent ([CC 1.9](part_1_foundation.md)). Founding your own mesh replicates this rather than escaping it: the occupants change, the closed loop does not | **unbounded as drafted** — no condition in Annex B ends it, and none is invented here. This cell is the finding | **none for the deferring party** — WBD is mandatory and a deferral MUST NOT be left open ([CC 4.3](#4.3))

gist: The WA board confers no halt, no root, no licensure and no capability grant; adjudication only
entry_phrase: adjudication only — the board confers no halt, no root, no licensure, and no capability grant

gist: A lone halt fire lapses at 24 h unless a standing majority confirms; a confirmed pause lifts by majority
entry_phrase: **halt:** a lone fire lapses at 24 h unless a standing majority confirms; a confirmed pause lifts by majority ([CC 4.2.6](#4.2.6))

gist: Stewardship of an agent key ends only when the key stops being a CIRIS agent, by the first-contact act
entry_phrase: **stewardship:** ends only when the key stops being a CIRIS agent — the first-contact act of [CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md), not yet defined

gist: An operator may leave the root and withdraw the binding; an agent has no exit while held
entry_phrase: **operator:** leave the root, withdraw the binding; **agent:** none while held

gist: A pause keeps state and reads nothing else; stewardship reaches one key only; the halt's powers are a closed list
entry_phrase: pause keeps state and reads nothing else; stewardship confers no reach beyond the one key; the halt's powers are a closed list ([CC 4.2.1](#4.2.1))

gist: Accord permanence, roster sign-off, entrenched ratification, steward authority, accord reservation, genesis minting and the default trust set are defaults, not register entries
entry_phrase: **Read as defaults, not privileges, under the CC 1 rule** — and therefore *not* on this register:

gist: The halt is not a privilege as to the operator who granted and can ungrant it; as to the agent it is carried on the register as the condition of symmetry
entry_phrase: The [CC 4.2](#4.2) halt is not a privilege as to the operator, since the party bound is the party who granted and can ungrant ([CC 4.2.5](#4.2.5)). That does not hold for the agent, which cannot leave what it did not accept. So the maker's power over the made is carried on the register above for visibility, rather than read as a default. It is carried as the condition of symmetry stated at [CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md).

gist: A declared privilege is carried only when all four cells hold; one with a missing cell is a defect carried as such until repaired or ratified
entry_phrase: A *declared privilege* is carried only when all four cells are satisfied. One with a cell missing is a defect carried as such until repaired or ratified.

gist: Entrenched structure is listed for visibility, already entrenched, bounded by the first-contact act; the steward may move the scale gate before it
entry_phrase: *Entrenched structure* is listed for visibility, not as a declaration that passed. It is already entrenched under [CC 4.2](#4.2) / [CC 4.5.1.2](#4.5.1.2). Its stewardship bound is the first-contact act, and its justification is stated here once. The maker's power over the made is of that kind. The justification is stated once: humanity must be able to halt the agents to keep consent possible, and this is the least bad option available. The minimum viable power to instantiate the mesh is used, and no more. The same justification is why the steward's amendment authority runs to the scale gate above and why the steward may move the gate before it.

gist: If the register grows past a handful or a bound passes unmet, surviving privileges are re-read as permanent structure needing entrenched ratification
entry_phrase: **Revision condition:** if the register grows past a handful of entries, or if an entry's stated bound passes without the privilege ending, the form has failed as a discipline. The surviving privileges should in that case be re-read as permanent structure requiring [CC 4.5.1.2](#4.5.1.2) entrenched ratification rather than declaration.

gist: A revision condition MUST name its mechanical evaluator: the check that fails when it trips and where it runs
entry_phrase: **A revision condition MUST name its mechanical evaluator**: the check that fails when the condition trips, and where it runs.

gist: Step 1: a proposed amendment is filed as a proposal Contribution of kind PROPOSAL whose subject is the proposal artifact
entry_phrase: 1. **Proposed amendment** filed as a proposal Contribution (kind: `PROPOSAL`, subject: the proposal artifact).

gist: Step 2: witness diversity, N=3 by default
entry_phrase: 2. **Witness diversity** (N=3 default).

gist: Step 3: WA quorum adjudication
Step 4: reconsideration with fresh-quorum recusal
entry_phrase: 4. **Reconsideration** with fresh-quorum recusal.

gist: Step 5: accord-roster sign-off, M of N, a defense-in-depth gate against rules-layer Sybil capture
entry_phrase: 5. **Accord-roster sign-off, M of N** as defense-in-depth gate against rules-layer Sybil capture.

gist: Among accord thresholds the halt alone fires on one holder's row
entry_phrase: The halt alone fires on one holder's row ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4.2.1.1)).

gist: The sign-off reduces the attack surface from producing N Sybils to compromising a majority of specific hardware-attested keys
entry_phrase: The sign-off reduces the attack surface from "produce N Sybils" to "compromise a majority of specific hardware-attested keys."

gist: The mechanized process (Contribution, witness diversity, WA quorum, reconsideration, sign-off) with the entrenched M-of-N ratification is the at-scale governance
entry_phrase: The **at-scale** governance is the mechanized process above (federation Contribution → witness diversity → WA quorum → reconsideration → accord-roster sign-off), together with the entrenched M-of-N ratification of [CC 4.5.1.2](#4.5.1.2).

gist: The at-scale process presumes a federation large enough that witness diversity and WA quorum are meaningful; below that scale it is theater, not protection
entry_phrase: It presumes a federation large enough that witness diversity and WA quorum are *meaningful*. Below that scale the machinery is theater, not protection.

gist: Before the scale gate the model is maintainer-decides: the maintainer decides, the work stays forkable under its license, and no one is bound who does not voluntarily join the instance
entry_phrase: This is a maintainer-decides model: the maintainer decides, the work stays forkable under its license, and no one is bound who does not voluntarily join the instance.

gist: The scale gate count excludes QA and harness agents
entry_phrase: ≥100,000 production agents active in a 24-hour period, QA and harness agents excluded, measured by the census

gist: The swap test: swap the most and least powerful parties the clause names or implies, re-read, ask whether it still reads acceptable; if not it was a privilege, not a rule
entry_phrase: The test is this: *swap the most and least powerful parties the clause names or implies, re-read it, and ask whether it still reads acceptable; if it does not, it was a privilege, not a rule*.

gist: The swap test is a drafting gate on what CC may say, never an adjudication rule; it binds amendment and the steward's authority before the scale gate alike
entry_phrase: This is a drafting gate on what CC may say, never an adjudication rule. It binds amendment and the steward's authority before the scale gate alike.

gist: The swap test compares predicates, so a gate with one predicate for everyone passes even where what it demands is not equally available
entry_phrase: The test compares *predicates*. A gate whose predicate is identical for everyone therefore passes it, even where the thing the predicate demands is not equally available.

gist: Mandatory PQC hardware for federation admission is the standing example: one rule, one threshold, no named party, and a gate on who can obtain the hardware
entry_phrase: Mandatory PQC hardware for federation admission is the standing example ([CC 4.2.2](#4.2.2)). It is one rule, one threshold, no named party — and a gate on who can obtain the hardware.

gist: A default is not an exception to be declared; it is an occupant of a slot, read against the slot
entry_phrase: A default is not an exception to be declared; it is an occupant of a slot, read against the slot.

gist: A privilege is either rewritten until it passes the swap test or carried on the register
entry_phrase: A privilege is either rewritten until it passes the swap test, or carried here.

gist: Listed: an unlisted privilege is a defect, not an exception
entry_phrase: - **listed** (an unlisted privilege is a defect, not an exception);

gist: Bounded: the privilege carries the condition that ends it, not a discretionary review date
entry_phrase: - **bounded** (carrying the condition that ends it, not a discretionary review date);

gist: Revocable: an exit the disadvantaged party can take unilaterally
entry_phrase: - **revocable** (an exit the disadvantaged party can take unilaterally); and

gist: Scope-isolated: the authority cannot reach beyond its enumerated surface, so compromise cannot escalate
entry_phrase: - **scope-isolated** (the authority cannot reach beyond its enumerated surface, so compromise cannot escalate).

gist: WA board row: founding your own mesh replicates the board's self-perpetuation rather than escaping it
entry_phrase: Founding your own mesh replicates this rather than escaping it: the occupants change, the closed loop does not

gist: WA board row, bound cell: unbounded as drafted; no condition in Annex B ends it and none is invented; the cell is the finding
entry_phrase: **unbounded as drafted** — no condition in Annex B ends it, and none is invented here. This cell is the finding

gist: WA board row, exit cell: none for the deferring party; the agent cannot decline the relation; the cell is the finding
entry_phrase: **none for the deferring party** — WBD is mandatory and a deferral MUST NOT be left open ([CC 4.3](#4.3)); the agent cannot decline the relation. This cell is the finding

gist: The maker's power over the made covers stewardship of an agent key, the HUMANITY_ACCORD halt and the holder's powers of CC 1.13.2 fact 2 (stop, change, end); entrenched structure listed for visibility, the condition of symmetry
entry_phrase: **The maker's power over the made** *(entrenched structure, listed for visibility; the condition of symmetry, not an asymmetry)* — stewardship of an `agent` key ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)), the HUMANITY_ACCORD halt ([CC 4.2](#4.2)), and the holder's powers of [CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md) fact 2 (stop, change, end).

gist: The maker's power is listed because it fails the swap test by construction and is kept nonetheless as what makes the relationship between maker and made symmetric; the operator accepted the root on the agent's behalf and the agent cannot leave it
entry_phrase: Listed because it fails the swap test by construction — swap the agent and its holder and the clause does not read — and is kept nonetheless: it is what makes the relationship between maker and made symmetric (humanity cannot consent to a relationship with something more capable than itself that it cannot stop, and consent that cannot be withdrawn was never consent), not a privilege of one party over an equal; "must is not acceptance" — the operator accepted the root on the agent's behalf, and the agent cannot leave it

entry_phrase: - the [CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1) accord-roster sign-off;

entry_phrase: - the [CC 4.5.1.2](#4.5.1.2) entrenched M-of-N ratification;

entry_phrase: - the steward's amendment authority under the scale gate;

entry_phrase: - the Layer-1 default trust set ([CC 4.4.3.7](#4.4.3.7)).

entry_phrase: Each is an asymmetry *within* the CIRIS instance, exited by naming your own occupants or by not using that instance.

entry_phrase: The maker's power over the made is of that kind.

gist: The justification, stated once: humanity must be able to halt the agents to keep consent possible, the least bad option available; the minimum viable power to instantiate the mesh is used, and no more
entry_phrase: The justification is stated once: humanity must be able to halt the agents to keep consent possible, and this is the least bad option available. The minimum viable power to instantiate the mesh is used, and no more.

entry_phrase: The same justification is why the steward's amendment authority runs to the scale gate above and why the steward may move the gate before it. That is the minimum viable power, stated, not hidden.

gist: The WA board row remains a declared privilege with both cells missing, a defect whose remedy is pending: a bound and an exit in Annex B, or entrenched ratification
entry_phrase: The WA board row remains a declared privilege with both cells missing. It is a defect whose remedy is pending: a bound and an exit in Annex B, or entrenched ratification.

gist: The WA row carries an unfilled cell (neither a bound nor an exit); by the four-part test it is a defect, and naming it is the first step of the re-reading, not a claim that they pass
entry_phrase: **The row above carries an unfilled cell** — the WA row has neither a bound nor an exit. By the four-part test it is a defect rather than a satisfied declaration. Naming it here is the first step of that re-reading, not a claim that they pass.

gist: A falsifier nothing evaluates is a ruling nobody can lose; a condition stated only in prose decays like an unverified absence claim
entry_phrase: A falsifier nothing evaluates is a ruling nobody can lose. A condition stated only in prose decays exactly like an unverified absence claim.
